answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by making each identity earn trust through a costly, verifiable work history before it can transact at full weight. A newcomer may wander in freely, but it starts with almost no standing: it must complete small, checked jobs, like a sonnet built line by line, before larger counterparties accept it. Attackers who mint thousands of copies face the same timber-by-timber cost for each one, paying real compute and time per fake, while one honest identity compounds a single durable reputation that cheap copies can never borrow.
